name: Simulated Clinical Trials
title: Simulated Clinical Trials
answer: Simulated clinical trials use computational models of patients, diseases, and treatments to predict how a drug might perform before or instead of a traditional human trial. They include virtual patient cohorts, synthetic control arms, and in silico dose-finding studies. In drug discovery they are used to prioritize compounds, refine trial inclusion criteria, and estimate effect sizes. The field sits within molecular simulation and quantitative systems pharmacology, and is tracked here as part of the AI Physician.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Simulated clinical trials use computational models of patients, diseases, and treatments to predict how a drug might perform before or instead of a traditional human trial. They include virtual patient cohorts, synthetic control arms, and in silico dose-finding studies. In drug discovery they are used to prioritize compounds, refine trial inclusion criteria, and estimate effect sizes. The field sits within molecular simulation and quantitative systems pharmacology, and is tracked here as part of the AI Physician.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on high performance computing clusters and cloud GPU instances, because simulating thousands of virtual patients requires repeated numerical integration of physiological models. Inputs include electronic health records, clinical trial data, genomic and proteomic profiles, and published pharmacokinetic parameters. Data are typically stored in versioned repositories with standardized formats such as CDISC or OMOP to allow reuse across studies. Many groups use containerized workflows to keep model dependencies reproducible.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Mechanistic approaches use quantitative systems pharmacology and physiologically based pharmacokinetic models to represent organ-level biology and drug exposure. Machine learning methods train on historical patient-level data to generate synthetic patients or predict outcomes under counterfactual treatment arms. Agent-based models simulate interactions among cells, tissues, or individuals to capture emergent disease behavior. Hybrid workflows combine mechanistic priors with learned parameters, then run Monte Carlo or Bayesian simulations to quantify uncertainty in trial endpoints.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The main rights and risk questions concern patient data provenance, consent for secondary use, and bias in synthetic populations that may underrepresent certain groups. Regulators expect evidence that simulated results match real trial outcomes before accepting them as support for a claim. If a model error leads to a harmful trial design or missed safety signal, liability may attach to the developer or sponsor; this site tracks six active product liability and wrongful death lawsuits against AI companies as a measure of that emerging risk. Documentation of training data, model version, and validation set is becoming standard practice.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Simulated trials are moving toward qualified regulatory use for dose selection, pediatric extrapolation, and rare disease studies where traditional enrollment is difficult. Digital twins of individual patients may allow personalized trial simulations that adapt a protocol in real time. Hybrid designs that combine a small human cohort with a large synthetic control arm are being tested for feasibility. Over time, the goal is to reduce unnecessary human exposure and animal testing while preserving statistical rigor.
